gaps.sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.

gaps.sentence: He joined ___ army when he was eighteen.
gaps.explanation: Institutions take 'the': the army, the police, the church.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

gaps.sentence: He found ___ coin buried in the sand.
gaps.explanation: 'A coin' first mention; 'in the sand' — sand as a mass takes 'the' here (the sand on that beach).

gaps.sentence: They sailed across ___ Mediterranean last summer.
gaps.explanation: Seas and oceans take 'the': the Mediterranean.

gaps.sentence: I saw ___ film last night, and the film was about mountain climbers.
gaps.hint: first mention of one of many
gaps.explanation: First mention of a countable noun takes 'a'; the second mention becomes 'the' (already written out here).

gaps.sentence: ___ young woman at reception speaks five languages.
gaps.explanation: 'The young woman at reception' — defined by the location phrase.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.
